terms.sub: Primordial Respiratory Diverticulum and Germ Layer Origins
clues: A ventral midline outgrowth appearing on the floor of the caudal foregut during week 4.
Its endodermal lining gives rise to the epithelium of the larynx, trachea, bronchi, and alveoli.
It elongates caudally and bifurcates into left and right primary bronchial buds.
A longitudinal partition formed during week 4 by midline fusion of bilateral foregut ridges.
It divides the cranial foregut into a ventral laryngotracheal tube and a dorsal esophagus.
Posterior deviation of this partition causes proximal esophageal atresia with a distal fistula.
The histological phase of lung development spanning weeks 5 through 17 of gestation.
On microscopic sections, the branching epithelial tubules surrounded by mesenchyme resemble an exocrine gland.
All conducting airways down to terminal bronchioles form, but no gas-exchanging structures exist yet.
The histological period of lung maturation spanning weeks 16 through 25.
Terminal bronchioles divide into respiratory bronchioles and alveolar ducts as capillaries invade the mesenchyme.
Type II pneumocytes begin secreting surfactant near the end of this stage, establishing the viability threshold.
A cuboidal septal epithelial cell situated at the corners of pulmonary alveoli containing lamellar bodies.
It serves as the stem cell progenitor that divides and differentiates into squamous type I alveolar cells.
It synthesizes and secretes dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine to prevent alveolar collapse.
A thick plate of mesoderm situated between the thoracic cavity and the yolk sac stalk during week 4.
It initially lies opposite cervical somites C3–C5 before migrating caudally to the thoracoabdominal junction.
It forms the central tendon of the adult diaphragm.
A life-threatening neonatal malformation most commonly resulting from failure of the left pleuroperitoneal membrane to close.
Abdominal viscera herniate into the hemithorax, producing a scaphoid abdomen and mediastinal shift.
Its primary cause of mortality is severe ipsilateral and contralateral pulmonary hypoplasia.
A congenital mass of non-functioning embryonic lung tissue lacking connection to the normal tracheobronchial tree.
It arises from a supernumerary caudal foregut lung bud.
It receives an anomalous systemic arterial supply directly from the thoracic or abdominal aorta.
A congenital posterior nasal airway obstruction caused by persistence of the embryonic oronasal membrane.
Affected neonates exhibit cyclical cyanosis that worsens during feeding and improves when crying.
It is a classic component of the multi-system CHARGE association.
